title: Pregnant Journalist Alleges Rahul Gandhi Pulled Her Hand at Protest
excerpt: Richa Parashar says she fell down steps and was hospitalised after covering the INDIA bloc march in Delhi; the BJP has taken up her charge and the Congress has rejected it as propaganda.
body:
• Journalist Richa Parashar, who says she is three months pregnant, alleges Rahul Gandhi grabbed and pulled her hand during the INDIA bloc protest in Delhi on October 12, after which his security pushed her and she fell down steps.
  • Parashar says she fell on her stomach, injured her hand and knees, and broke her phone, and she was later taken to hospital.
  • The BJP has accused Gandhi of manhandling her and its leaders visited her in hospital; Congress leader Alka Lamba rejected the allegation and called it BJP propaganda.
  • Congress supporters have shared videos of the commotion arguing the footage does not clearly show Gandhi pushing her; no independent finding has been reported.

A journalist who says she is three months pregnant has alleged that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi grabbed her hand and pulled her forward while she was covering the INDIA bloc's protest in New Delhi on October 12, and that his security personnel then pushed her, sending her down a set of steps. The allegation, reported by The Times of India and DY365, has set off a political row, with the Congress rejecting her account outright.

The journalist's account

Richa Parashar said she had extended her microphone toward Gandhi during the protest when she was signalled to move it, and that she put it forward again as other journalists' microphones were also being pushed aside. In a video recorded from her hospital bed, she alleged that Gandhi moved toward her, grabbed her hand and pulled her forward, and that his bodyguards then pushed her. She said she fell down the stairs at the Supreme Court premises, landing on her face and stomach.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PsYyaVvjbLg

Parashar said her cameraperson was also pushed and fell on top of her, followed by several other people in the crowd. She reported injuries to her hand and knees and said her phone broke in the fall. She added that she had not asked Gandhi any question at the time, alleged that his supporters shouted at her rather than helping her up, and asked media organisations that recorded the incident to release their footage.

"pushed by the man who says Smash the Patriarchy"

— Richa Parashar, journalist, in an Instagram video

BJP takes up the charge, Congress rejects it

The BJP accused Gandhi of manhandling the journalist. Spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari alleged that Gandhi grabbed her and pushed her to the ground, said she had been hospitalised, and noted that BJP leaders had visited her. Delhi BJP vice-president Rajesh Bhatia said Parashar's sister contacted him on Monday evening seeking medical help, and BJP MLA Umang Bajaj condemned the alleged conduct, saying public representatives should answer journalists' questions rather than manhandle them.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2109918638002364599

Congress leader Alka Lamba rejected the allegations in a post on X, accusing the BJP of manufacturing propaganda. She questioned the timeline of the incident and of Parashar's hospital visit, and raised questions about an X-ray reportedly being conducted despite Parashar saying she was pregnant. Other Congress leaders and supporters shared videos of the commotion, arguing that the footage did not clearly show Gandhi pushing Parashar. The Congress has denied that the incident occurred as described.

The protest behind the incident

The alleged incident took place during the INDIA bloc's march in Delhi over the revision of electoral rolls, at which opposition parties have demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The march itself — a coordinated opposition protest against the voter-roll exercise — had already drawn national attention before the allegation shifted the focus to the treatment of a journalist covering it.

What happens next

The competing accounts turn on video evidence. Parashar has asked news organisations present at the scene to release their recordings, and Congress supporters are circulating clips they say do not show a push. Until fuller footage or an official inquiry settles what happened in the crowd that day, the allegation and the denial stand unreconciled — and the episode has become the latest flashpoint in the fight between the Congress and the BJP over the voter-roll protest.
